key_insight: PolyGPT generates highly valid polymer structures, but electrolyte conditioning increases repetition and reduces the yield of distinct polymers satisfying combined design requests.
engineering_relevance: Polymer electrolyte screening should prioritize distinct, novel candidates meeting design constraints rather than property-prediction error alone.
method: Use a 38.3-million-parameter decoder-only Transformer to generate polymer repeat units.
Condition generation on optional property targets, chemical-feature inclusion or exclusion, and electrolyte-domain requests.
Compare generation conditions using the validation-loss-selected model and assess nine checkpoints.
evidence_signal: At a Tg target of 246.11 K, electrolyte conditioning slightly improved predictor-estimated MAE from 26.97 to 26.07 K but reduced distinct-valid yield within 50 K from 82.35% to 32.31% of attempts.
watch_item: Reported Tg accuracy is predictor-estimated, not experimental validation, and checkpoint selection by validation loss may miss models with better distinct, catalog-unseen candidate yield.
paper_title: PolyGPT: A Decoder-Only Transformer for Polymer Electrolyte Design
